In this RTX 4070 vs RX 7800 XT comparison, we break down the strengths and weaknesses of two of the most talked‑about mid‑range GPUs for 2024 gaming. Whether you’re building a new rig or upgrading an existing one, understanding how these cards stack up in real‑world scenarios will help you make an informed purchase. Below we dive into specs, performance, power draw, pricing, and the extras that can tip the scales.

## Performance Overview
### 1080p Gaming
At 1080p, both cards deliver buttery smooth frame rates in most modern titles. The RTX 4070 tends to edge out the RX 7800 XT by roughly 5‑10 % in rasterization‑heavy games thanks to its higher boost clock and efficient Ada Lovelace architecture. However, the RX 7800 XT often matches or slightly exceeds the 4070 in titles that are heavily optimized for AMD’s RDNA 3 pipeline, such as certain esports shooters.

### 1440p Gaming
Moving to 1440p, the gap narrows. The RTX 4070’s DLSS 3 frame generation can push average FPS well above 100 in supported games, while the RX 7800 XT relies on FSR 3, which, although improving, still lags behind DLSS in image quality and latency reduction. In native rasterization without upscaling, the two cards are virtually neck‑and‑neck, with differences usually under 3 %.

### 4K Gaming
At 4K, both GPUs start to feel the strain. The RTX 4070’s 12 GB of GDDR6X memory gives it a slight advantage in memory‑bound scenarios, allowing it to maintain playable frame rates in more demanding titles when paired with DLSS. The RX 7800 XT’s 16 GB of GDDR6 helps in texture‑heavy games, but without a strong upscaling solution, average FPS often drops below 60 in the latest AAA releases.

## Architecture Differences
### GPU Core Specs
The RTX 4070 is built on NVIDIA’s Ada Lovelace architecture, featuring 5888 CUDA cores, a base clock of ~1920 MHz and a boost that can reach ~2475 MHz. The RX 7800 XT uses AMD’s RDNA 3 design, packing 3840 stream processors with a game clock around 2125 MHz and a boost up to ~2430 MHz. While core counts differ, IPC improvements on both sides keep performance competitive.

### Memory Configuration
NVIDIA equips the 4070 with 12 GB of GDDR6X running at 21 Gbps over a 192‑bit bus, yielding ~504 GB/s bandwidth. AMD provides the 7800 XT with 16 GB of GDDR6 at 18 Gbps over a 256‑bit bus, delivering about 576 GB/s bandwidth. The larger frame buffer on the AMD card can benefit texture‑heavy workloads, while the faster GDDR6X on the NVIDIA side helps in latency‑sensitive scenarios.

## Power & Thermals
### TDP Comparison
The RTX 4070 carries a rated TDP of 200 W, whereas the RX 7800 XT is rated at 263 W. In practice, the 4070 typically draws 180‑190 W under load, while the 7800 XT often sits between 230‑250 W. This difference translates to lower electricity costs
